what_its_for: Zanamivir is an antiviral medicine used to treat influenza (the flu) in adults and children who are at least 7 years old. It can also help prevent the flu in people who are at least 5 years old. It works best when started within 2 days of your flu symptoms beginning.
how_to_take: Zanamivir comes as a powder that you breathe in (inhale) using a special device called a Diskhaler. Before using it for the first time, ask your pharmacist or doctor to show you how to load and use the Diskhaler properly. Always inhale the powder through your mouth — do not swallow it. Do not use zanamivir with a nebulizer or mechanical ventilator. If you also use an inhaler for asthma or other breathing problems (like a bronchodilator), use that bronchodilator FIRST before using zanamivir. Do not puncture the blister until you are ready to use it.
dosing: For TREATING the flu (age 7 and older): Inhale 2 blisters (10 mg total) twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening — for 5 days. The two doses each day should be spaced about 12 hours apart. For PREVENTING the flu (age 5 and older): Inhale 2 blisters (10 mg total) once a day for 10 days (or up to 28 days if your doctor prescribes it). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are taking it twice a day and you remember the missed dose on the same day, take it right away and then take your next dose at the usual time.
storage: Store zanamivir Rotadisks at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not refrigerate or freeze. Keep the Diskhaler device dry and clean. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not use zanamivir in a nebulizer or any breathing machine — this can cause the device to malfunction and may be dangerous. Avoid skipping doses, as this can make the medicine less effective. If you have asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), be very careful — zanamivir can cause sudden, serious breathing problems in people with lung disease. Do not receive a live nasal flu vaccine (FluMist) within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after taking zanamivir, as it may make the vaccine less effective.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: sudden wheezing, shortness of breath, or trouble breathing after using zanamivir; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; unusual behavior, confusion, hallucinations, or agitation (especially in children); seizures; or if your flu symptoms get worse or do not improve after 5 days of treatment. Also call your doctor if you develop new symptoms or a high fever returns.
when_it_works: Zanamivir works best when started within 48 hours (2 days) of your first flu symptoms. It will not cure the flu but can shorten how long you feel sick by about 1 to 2 days and may reduce the severity of your symptoms. It does NOT treat colds or other viral infections — only the flu.
special_populations: Asthma or COPD patients: Use with great caution. Your doctor may decide this medicine is not safe for you because it can cause sudden, serious breathing problems. If your doctor does prescribe it, have a fast-acting bronchodilator (rescue inhaler) nearby at all times. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before using zanamivir. It should only be used during pregnancy if the benefits clearly outweigh the risks. Breastfeeding mothers: It is not known if zanamivir passes into breast milk. Ask your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is usually needed, but older adults with kidney or liver problems should talk to their doctor. Children under 7 (for treatment) or under 5 (for prevention): Zanamivir is not approved for these age groups.
